New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-older-apis-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-older-apis-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-legacy-apis.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/older-apis`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/older-apis, old raw lines 8-25 and 27-34 and new raw lines 9-26 and 28-35 establish the same guidance. Stripe no longer updates documentation for some replaced APIs and recommends Payment Intents, Setup Intents and Payment Methods for new features and migration. Both captures require migration for local payment methods using Sources, identify shutdown as a plan and point to later email information, and describe Sources card support as deprecated without a current shutoff plan on this route. They put Charges and old ACH under unsupported APIs still usable until an existing integration upgrades. The matrix groups the modern APIs as broader in payment methods and supporting SCA readiness, Terminal and future development, while the Charges, Tokens and Sources group lists cards and ACH and lacks those capabilities. The overview contains no account prerequisites, API minimum or runtime evidence. A PaymentIntent tracks a payment, SetupIntent saves for future use without charging, PaymentMethod represents an instrument and Charge records a specific attempt, according to the linked implementation context. In the November Charges card example, Stripe.js tokenizes card details in the browser. The merchant sends that Token to its server, which creates the Charge. Separately, both dated transition guides allow legacy Source creation on the front end or server. Tokenization and Source creation are preparatory steps. Charge creation is separate, and fulfillment depends on verified payment success. In the newer Intent path, the server creates the Intent and handles status verification itself or via server webhooks, while the client can handle authentication with the client secret. See April transition lines 26-46, November transition lines 27-49 and November Charges lines 27-41. source-stripe-legacy-apis.md already distinguishes November Charges card-payment creation from Charge reads and refunds, but its April-only older-APIs attribution omits the November repetition, its Sources card status lacks reciprocal context from the November Sources transition, and legacy ACH continued use needs the dedicated no-new-users qualification.

Capture metadata, comparison-table spacing and SCA Markdown emphasis changed. The matrix values, migration links and caveats stayed the same, so the raw warrants no substantive update. source-stripe-legacy-apis.md independently needs a correction. Add reciprocal warnings for November’s contemporaneous dedicated Charges notice (planned removal of card-payment creation and a new-integration payment-creation bar) and its Sources transition notice (planned removal of Sources card acceptance and legacy Cards support, required migration and email follow-up), alongside the broader Sources new-integration ban. Keep the older ACH continued-use claim paired with the November ACH guide’s new-onboarding block. The grouped Older APIs matrix lists Cards/ACH for Charges, Tokens and Sources (old raw lines 27-34 and new raw lines 28-35). The separate April 20 Charges comparison says legacy Charges supported cards and all methods on the Sources API (raw/stripe-charges-vs-payment-intents-2025.md lines 24-29). Preserve both scopes and dates. The matrix gives a grouped comparison, while the April statement describes the historical Charges/Sources route under its own conditions. Neither overrides the November Charges creation bar or the November Sources migration and new-integration restrictions. The November card-oriented transition, raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-transitioning-2026-11-07.md lines 39-49, describes incomplete authorization and server retrieval or server webhook verification without restating a 48-hour timeout. The captures leave a current universal timeout unresolved. The 2019-02-11 status names belong to the April migration guide and the overview supplies no API/SDK minimum, shutdown date or runtime success proof.

source_assessments.reason: A reader asking whether omission always rejects or defaults a payment instrument could mispredict the actual create request or charge an unintended default. A reader following the raw save route sees both automatic and explicit attachment in one flow and could act twice. The summary needs to state the narrow create exception and qualifying attachment behavior directly rather than leaving a conflict between linked passages. Without the warning, a reader following the still-visible Button instructions on an Endive integration can choose an Element creation call that throws.

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/migration, the November and April 20, 2026 guides describe staged migration of an existing cards/Charges integration. Update the API/client library as applicable, use compatible Charge-property readers where needed, migrate web or the separately linked mobile flow, migrate saved cards, and test authentication in a sandbox. The guide recommends the latest API and library, with pre-2019-02-11 `requires_source` and `requires_source_action` corresponding to `requires_payment_method` and `requires_action` (old raw lines 10-27, new raw lines 11-28). The server creates a PaymentIntent and exposes its client secret to the client. Stripe.js `confirmCardPayment` initiates Charge creation; the dated Payment Request Button path passes the token ID and separately invokes its callback when the confirmation promise resolves. With automatic confirmation, fulfill server-side after `payment_intent.succeeded` (old raw lines 29-106, new raw lines 30-106). To save during checkout, supply a Customer and `setup_future_usage` for on-session only or off-session/both. The resulting PaymentMethod saves after confirmation and required actions. To save without an initial charge, create a SetupIntent, use its client secret with `confirmCardSetup`, and use the resulting PaymentMethod ID for Customer attachment where needed (old raw lines 119-168, new raw lines 120-169). For a later charge, explicitly pass both the Customer and desired Card, Source or PaymentMethod IDs and flag off-session when applicable. List saved methods via the Payment Methods API since new PaymentMethods are absent from `customer.sources` (old raw lines 170-178, new raw lines 171-179). `source-stripe-legacy-apis.md` lines 126-135 captures the main steps but needs the conditional attachment and distinct create API fallback made explicit.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/migration, the underlying April and November migration flow is unchanged. November changes the Payment Element quickstart URL, removes the API upgrade fragment, and tidies numbering, headings and tables (old raw lines 6-27, new raw lines 7-28, old raw lines 180-191 and new raw lines 181-192). The separately captured linked quickstart describes Checkout Sessions with Payment Element, while the dated card Elements procedures use `confirmCardPayment` with a PaymentIntent. Preserve the old version status names, server/client and webhook boundaries, and sandbox-only test outcomes. In `source-stripe-legacy-apis.md` and the Payment Intents route, scope parallel Charges operation to migrating an existing integration. The separate November Charges page lines 15-25 deprecates card payment creation and bars new integrations from creating payments through Charges without giving a removal date. Preserve the guide’s explicit saved instrument choice and separately warn that the November create API lines 647-650 documents legacy `customer.default_source` fallback specifically when `payment_method` is omitted with `confirm=true`. Both dated guides describe automatic attachment with a Customer and `setup_future_usage` after confirmation and required actions, then include an attach instruction. Use the create and confirm API conditions to avoid implying a required second attach. Separate no-payment SetupIntent success, later off-session PaymentIntent confirmation and actual paid fulfillment (old raw lines 132-178 and new raw lines 133-179). The Payment Request Button procedure and Express Checkout Element alternative persist in both migration captures (old raw lines 66-105 and new raw lines 67-106). A separate November Button page marks the Element deprecated and points to the Express Checkout Element migration guide. The September 30, 2026 Endive changelog says `elements.create('paymentRequestButton')` throws beginning with Endive, including React `PaymentRequestButtonElement`, while Stripe.js versions through Dahlia continue to support the Element. Preserve the token and callback workflow as dated evidence and add the warning alongside its legacy source route, with direct reciprocal links from the Payment Intents source list and Express Checkout Element migration notes. The Element-specific removal does not establish removal of lower-level Payment Request or `confirmCardPayment`, wallet eligibility, or a verified migration.
